era: The Fall of Goma and Bukavu (Jan–Feb 2025)

events.title: M23 Cuts Roads, Encircles Goma
events.detail: M23 rebels, which UN experts say are backed by Rwandan special forces, cut the two main roads into Goma and pushed toward the North Kivu capital, forcing FARDC and allied SADC (SAMIDRC) troops into defensive positions around the city.

events.title: M23 Captures Goma, Provincial Capital of North Kivu
events.detail: M23 fighters entered Goma on January 27 amid a chaotic FARDC retreat. A prison break at Munzenze prison and days of urban fighting left an estimated 2,000–3,000 dead, including 13–17 South African SAMIDRC soldiers and Uruguayan and South African UN peacekeepers.

sources.name: News on Air / Government of India

events.confidenceReason: Death toll estimates ranged from ~787 (early WHO count) to nearly 3,000 (later UN estimate); figures were revised upward for weeks after the battle.

events.title: Protests and Embassy Attacks Rock Kinshasa Over Goma's Fall
events.detail: Protesters in Kinshasa, roughly 2,600 km from the front, attacked and looted the Rwandan embassy along with the US, French, Belgian and other diplomatic missions, venting anger at the government's failure to stop M23's advance on Goma.

events.title: UN: Death Toll From Goma Battle Nears 3,000
events.detail: A senior UN official said close to 3,000 people were killed during the battle for Goma, with roughly 2,000 bodies recovered from city streets and about 900 more counted in hospital morgues — one of the deadliest urban battles of the eastern DRC conflict.

events.title: M23 Forces Closure of Goma-Area IDP Camps
events.detail: M23 ordered residents of the Bulengo and Lushagala displacement camps, together hosting over 100,000 people, to leave within 72 hours. The WHO later found roughly 90 IDP sites in and around Goma destroyed or dismantled, affecting about 248,676 people.

events.title: M23 Captures Bukavu, Capital of South Kivu
events.detail: M23 fighters entered Bukavu, a city of 1.3 million people, with next to no resistance from a retreating FARDC. Some residents cheered the rebels while thousands fled toward Burundi — a second major blow to Kinshasa's authority in barely three weeks.

events.title: PM Suminwa: 7,000 Killed in Eastern DRC Since January
events.detail: Prime Minister Judith Suminwa told parliament that more than 7,000 people had been killed in fighting in eastern DRC since the start of the year, with roughly 3,000 of the deaths in Goma alone and thousands of bodies still unidentified.
events.confidenceReason: Figure is the DRC government's own tally; independent verification of a single eastern-DRC-wide total has not been possible given the scale of the crisis.

events.title: Bombing at M23 Rally Kills Several in Bukavu
events.detail: Explosions and gunfire struck a public gathering M23 had organized at Independence Square in Bukavu, killing several people and wounding dozens, days after the rebels had seized the square as a symbol of their control of the city.

era: Sanctions, Walikale, and the SAMIDRC Withdrawal (Mar–May 2025)

events.title: EU Sanctions Rwandan Officials and M23 Leaders
events.detail: The EU imposed asset freezes and travel bans on senior Rwandan officials — including the head of Rwanda's Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board — a gold-trading company, and several M23 leaders for their roles in the conflict and Congolese mineral trade. Rwanda responded by cutting diplomatic ties with Belgium.

events.title: SADC Summit Ends SAMIDRC Mission, Orders Withdrawal
events.detail: An extraordinary SADC Heads of State summit terminated the SAMIDRC military mission's mandate in eastern DRC following the fall of Goma and the loss of South African, Tanzanian and Malawian troops, and endorsed a phased withdrawal of the force.

events.title: M23 Captures Walikale, Its Furthest Westward Advance
events.detail: M23 fighters took the town of Walikale after seizing Kashebere and Kibati along the way, marking the rebels' deepest push west into North Kivu and threatening key road links toward Kisangani.

events.title: SADC Begins Phased Withdrawal of SAMIDRC Troops
events.detail: SADC officially began withdrawing SAMIDRC forces from eastern DRC, first repatriating equipment and logistics before personnel, transiting by road through Rwanda back to South Africa, Tanzania and Malawi.

events.title: Qatar Opens Direct Talks Between DRC Government and M23
events.detail: Qatar began hosting direct, Doha-based negotiations between Kinshasa and the AFC/M23 coalition, running in parallel with the separate US-brokered DRC-Rwanda track, after Angola stepped back from its role as African Union lead mediator.

era: The Washington Accords and Doha Ceasefire (Jun–Aug 2025)

events.title: DRC and Rwanda Sign Washington Accords
events.detail: Foreign ministers of the DRC and Rwanda signed the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity, committing Rwanda to disengage and withdraw forces from eastern DRC and the DRC to neutralize the FDLR, coupled with a regional economic integration plan tied to Congo's mineral wealth.

events.title: UN Experts: Rwanda Coltan Smuggling at "Unprecedented Levels"
events.detail: A UN Group of Experts report found Rwanda had backed M23 militarily and smuggled Congolese coltan — much of it from the Rubaya mine — into its own export chain at unprecedented levels, blending it with domestic ore before selling it into global electronics supply chains.

events.title: DRC and M23 Sign Doha Declaration of Principles
events.detail: The Congolese government and AFC/M23 signed a Declaration of Principles in Doha committing to a permanent ceasefire and direct negotiations, targeting a comprehensive peace accord by Aug 17, 2025 — a deadline that would ultimately slip by nearly four months.

events.title: ADF Kills 38–43 Civilians in Komanda Church Attack
events.detail: Islamic State-affiliated ADF (ISCAP) fighters attacked worshippers at a night vigil at Saint Anuarite Catholic church in Komanda, Ituri, stabbing and shooting at least 38–43 civilians to death — an attack MONUSCO linked to reprisals for a Ugandan-Congolese offensive on ADF's Madina camp.

events.title: FDLR Faction Signs Disarmament Protocol
events.detail: A faction of the Rwandan Hutu FDLR militia signed a memorandum committing to phased demobilization, disarmament and cantonment leading toward the group's dissolution — a key Washington Accords obligation on the DRC — though it demanded no forced repatriation to Rwanda.

era: The Doha Framework and Minerals Deal (Sep–Dec 2025)

events.title: DRC Lifts Eight-Month Cobalt Export Ban
events.detail: Kinshasa allowed cobalt exports to resume after an eight-month suspension first imposed in February 2025 to arrest a global price collapse; the halt had widened the DRC's current account deficit even as copper output continued to climb.

events.title: DRC and AFC/M23 Sign Doha Framework for Comprehensive Peace
events.detail: The two sides signed an eight-chapter framework addressing the conflict's root causes, intended as the basis for a full peace agreement targeted for summer 2026. The African Union welcomed the deal, though M23 offered no firm commitments on disarmament.

events.title: US and DRC Sign Strategic Minerals Partnership
events.detail: Washington and Kinshasa signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement giving US companies preferential access to Congolese cobalt, copper and coltan — the commercial complement to the Washington Accords that the Trump administration had pursued since Tshisekedi's February 2025 minerals-for-security offer.

events.title: Kagame and Tshisekedi Formally Sign Washington Accords
events.detail: Presidents Paul Kagame and Félix Tshisekedi signed the Washington Accords at a Washington ceremony hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio with President Trump as witness. Kagame credited Trump and Rubio for creating "a new and effective dynamism"; Tshisekedi pledged to honor the accord's terms.

events.title: AFC/M23 Captures Uvira, South Kivu's Southern Gateway
events.detail: AFC/M23 fighters took the Lake Tanganyika port city of Uvira after more than a week of fighting and the earlier capture of Sange, Luberizi, Luvungi and Kamanyola — the rebels' biggest territorial gain since February 2025 and a direct breach of the Doha ceasefire commitments.

events.title: UN Security Council Extends MONUSCO Mandate to December 2026
events.detail: The Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2808, extending the peacekeeping mission's mandate for another year, directing that any future drawdown be gradual and conditions-based, and narrowing MONUSCO's operational focus to North Kivu and Ituri.

era: Disaster at Rubaya and Renewed Fighting (Jan–Apr 2026)

events.title: Landslide Kills Over 200 at Rubaya Coltan Mine
events.detail: Heavy rains triggered two successive landslides at the Rubaya mine complex, burying artisanal miners in unstable pits. An initial confirmed toll of 227 dead rose past 400 within days as recovery crews struggled through mud, making it one of the deadliest mining disasters in DRC history.
events.confidenceReason: Initial toll of 227 rose to 400+ within days; mud and continued instability at the site prevented full recovery and a final count.

events.title: DRC Adds Rubaya to US Strategic Minerals Shortlist
events.detail: Days after the landslide disaster, Kinshasa added the M23-controlled Rubaya coltan site to a shortlist of strategic mineral assets for US investment under the December 2025 partnership, underscoring the tension between formalizing the mine and its continued taxation by the rebels.

events.title: Angolan-Proposed Ceasefire Collapses Within Days
events.detail: Tshisekedi agreed in principle to a ceasefire proposed by Angolan President João Lourenço, but M23 said it had not been properly consulted and remained committed only to the Doha process. Both sides accused each other of violations within days, and fighting resumed.

events.title: FARDC-Wazalendo Launch Masisi Offensive
events.detail: Congolese army units and allied Wazalendo militias opened a multi-axis offensive in southern Masisi, retaking villages including Miruta, Ngololo and the Katoyi group center — roughly 25 miles southwest of Rubaya — after four days of fighting.

events.title: FARDC Drone Strike Kills M23 Military Spokesman
events.detail: A Congolese army drone strike near Rubaya killed Willy Ngoma, a veteran M23 member serving as the group's military spokesman — the highest-profile M23 death of the Masisi counteroffensive.

events.title: M23 Counterattacks, Recaptures Masisi Villages
events.detail: M23 pushed Wazalendo fighters back from Kashovu and Lumbishi near the South Kivu border and, in the following days, recaptured a string of villages initially lost in the FARDC-Wazalendo offensive, illustrating the collapse of the Angolan ceasefire proposal.

events.title: US Sanctions Rwandan Army and Four Senior Commanders
events.detail: The US Treasury sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Force and four senior commanders over their support for M23 — a rare direct penalty on Rwanda's military establishment, imposed even as Washington continued to broker the Doha peace track.

events.title: OCHA: 14.9 Million People Need Humanitarian Aid in 2026
events.detail: The UN's humanitarian coordination office projected that 14.9 million people across the DRC would need humanitarian assistance in 2026, with food insecurity affecting 28 million nationwide amid continued fighting, cholera outbreaks and mass displacement in the east.

events.title: DRC Files Case Against Rwanda at the ICJ
events.detail: Kinshasa lodged a case at the International Court of Justice accusing Rwanda of responsibility for more than 30 years of atrocities in eastern DRC — massacres, sexual violence, torture and forced displacement — alleging breaches of the Genocide Convention and other treaties. The court rejected Rwanda's jurisdictional challenge the same day and ruled the case admissible, sending it to the merits phase.

events.title: Rwanda Rejects DRC's FDLR Disarmament Protocol
events.detail: Rwanda formally rejected the DRC-FDLR demobilization protocol as inconsistent with the Washington Accords' Concept of Operations, which required Kinshasa to neutralize the FDLR within 90 days rather than negotiate cantonment terms directly with the group.

events.title: African Union Adopts Six-Month Peace Roadmap
events.detail: African leaders adopted a six-month AU-led roadmap covering July–December 2026 to coordinate the overlapping Doha, Washington and SADC/EAC peace tracks, humanitarian access and verification mechanisms.

events.title: Washington Accords Joint Oversight Committee Meets in Paris
events.detail: The Joint Oversight Committee — comprising the DRC, Rwanda, the African Union facilitator, Qatar and the US — met in Paris to review implementation of the Washington Accords, with the next Joint Security Coordination Mechanism session set for Germany in mid-August.

events.title: Great Lakes Contact Group Presses DRC on FDLR Protocol
events.detail: The Great Lakes Contact Group urged the DRC to act on the stalled FDLR disarmament protocol, as the group's fate remained the central unresolved obligation blocking full implementation of the Washington Accords more than a year after signing.

events.title: Prisoner Exchange Held as Wazalendo-M23 Clash Near Kavumu
events.detail: The ICRC facilitated the transfer of 15 DRC-held M23 prisoners from Beni to M23-controlled Rutshuru, a Doha peace process mechanism that had stalled since April, even as M23 expelled a Congolese government member from the joint ceasefire verification mechanism and Wazalendo fighters clashed with M23 near Kavumu airport, north of Bukavu.

media.caption: ICRC-facilitated transfer of 15 DRC-held M23 prisoners from Beni to Rutshuru, Aug 7, 2026

events.title: DRC and Rwanda Hold Sixth JSCM Meeting in Geneva, Set October Planning Conference
events.detail: DRC and Rwandan delegations, with the US, Qatar, Togo (as AU mediator) and the AU Commission, held the sixth Joint Security Coordination Mechanism meeting at the US Mission in Geneva. The two governments agreed to two new initiatives to strengthen monitoring and verification of Washington Accords implementation, and to a trilateral planning conference in October 2026 to produce a revised Operations Order. The DRC also presented its FDLR Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration plan, followed by a virtual session with MONUSCO on its DDR operational experience. The next JSCM session is set for Sep 16-17 in Geneva.

events.title: AFC/M23-Wazalendo Fighting Spreads From Kalehe Into Masisi
events.detail: Clashes between AFC/M23 and pro-government Wazalendo fighters that began in early August around Bunje, Chabikere, Mpanama and Katale in Kalehe territory's Ziralo grouping (South Kivu), with FARDC accusing M23 of using 82mm mortars, continued through Aug 11-13 near Chambombo, Kazinga and Lumbishi. By Aug 17, fighting had spread into Masisi territory's Ufamandu I grouping (North Kivu), with heavy artillery fire reported around Remeka, Katuundu, Biriko and Kashovu villages. Several hundred families were displaced; pro-government and M23 sources disputed which side held the contested villages.

events.title: Fighting Widens Across Kalehe, Masisi and Walungu as M23 Recaptures Ziralo
events.detail: After pro-government forces briefly retook Chambombo and Lumbishi around Aug 12, M23 mounted a counteroffensive from Aug 15, recapturing a string of Ziralo-grouping villages including Tushunguti and controlling the entire grouping by Aug 19. Fighting also spread into Masisi's Ufamandu I grouping (Katuunda and Miko, Aug 18; Remeka, Aug 20) and, for the first time since May 2026, into Walungu territory, where Wazalendo fighters attacked M23 positions at Kaniola on Aug 13-14 and combat resumed near Luntukulu on Aug 20.

events.title: Drone Strikes Hit Mwalu Hotel in Fizi-Centre, Wounding Two Civilians
events.detail: Two TB2-type drones dropped bombs on the Mwalu Hotel in Fizi-Centre, South Kivu around 1 a.m. on Aug 19, seriously wounding two civilians, including the hotel manager, and causing heavy damage to the recently built hotel. FARDC's Sukola 2 South Kivu sector said the drones were piloted from Rwanda and called the strike a violation of international humanitarian law and the Washington Accords; attribution was not independently verified.
events.confidenceReason: FARDC attributes the strike to Rwandan-piloted drones; M23/Rwanda have not confirmed responsibility, and the account has not been independently verified.

events.title: FARDC Downs RDF/M23-Twirwaneho Drone Near Runyengo in the Fizi Highlands
events.detail: FARDC intercepted and destroyed a kamikaze drone attributed to Rwandan forces, M23 and the allied Twirwaneho/Red-Tabara militia near Runyengo, between Mukoko and Mulima villages in the Fizi highlands, around 8 a.m. on Aug 20 — hours after loyalist forces repelled rebel attacks on their highland positions, part of a wider pattern of drone activity over the tense South Kivu highlands front.

events.title: Pro-Government Forces and M23-Allied Twirwaneho Clash in the Minembwe Highlands
events.detail: Pro-government forces launched an offensive against M23-allied Twirwaneho fighters around Nyaruhinga and Mukoko in the Minembwe highlands of South Kivu; M23 counterattacked using KT-6 and OWA loitering drones. M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka said the bombings "caused civilian casualties and significant damage to civilian infrastructure," a claim not independently verified.
events.confidenceReason: M23's civilian-casualty claim for Minembwe bombings has not been independently corroborated by MONUSCO or humanitarian agencies.

events.title: DRC and M23 Agree Roadmap for Doha Peace Talks, Set Aug 24 EJVM+ Verification Mission
events.detail: Representatives of the DRC government and AFC/M23, with the US, Qatar, Togo (as AU mediator), the AU Commission and host Switzerland, met in Geneva Aug 17-21 and issued a joint statement establishing a roadmap of sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations under the Nov 2025 Doha Framework. The parties agreed to a standardized method for reporting ceasefire violations and welcomed progress operationalizing the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), including its Secretariat and an Aug 20 reconnaissance mission with MONUSCO logistical support ahead of the first EJVM+ ceasefire verification mission, scheduled for Aug 24 in Minembwe.

media.caption: DRC and M23 negotiators reached a roadmap for Doha peace talks after Geneva meetings, Aug 22, 2026

events.title: Civil Society: ADF Killed 2,400+ Civilians in Bapere Sector Over Two Years
events.detail: Local civil society in the Bapere sector of Lubero territory, North Kivu, said ADF/ISCAP fighters had killed more than 2,400 civilians since mid-2024, with the Manguredjipa axis among the hardest-hit zones and additional reports of kidnappings, arson and looting. Civil society president Samuel Kaheni cited joint FARDC-UPDF operations and Wazalendo engagement for a relative recent calm, while urging residents to share preventive intelligence with security forces.

media.caption: Aerial view of Luofu in Lubero territory, North Kivu, near the Bapere sector cited in the ADF toll report

events.confidenceReason: Figure is a local civil society tally presented Aug 18, 2026, not an independently verified UN or government count, though consistent with years of documented ADF/ISCAP violence in the area.
